newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt floats pensions-for-housing plan.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt floats pensions-for-housing plan.

text.p: The Australian government issued a discussion paper on Tuesday raising the prospect of allowing people to use their superannuation savings as a deposit to buy a home.
Treasury said in the discussion paper released with the 1997/98 budget it would invite submissions from all interested parties for consideration after June 30.
The conservative Liberal/National government raised the possibility of a pension-for-housing scheme during the March 1996 election campaign, but have yet to commit to it as policy.
Treasury said the paper aimed to assess the effects on national savings, retirment incomes and the government's fiscal position of such a scheme.
Currently savings in superannuation schemes, which are given a tax break, are not allowed to be withdrawn before retirement for use as deposit on a home.
A pension-for-housing scheme could have a dramatic effect on pension funds and the housing industry.

Large numbers of first-home buyers would be expected to withdraw money from their pension funds to put a deposit on new homes in particular, effectively channelling funds away from traditional investment markets into the housing construction market.
